summary: A deep dive into AppLovin (APP, AVOID) after the CEO claimed on a podcast the company could be worth a trillion dollars — requiring $30B+ in annual free cash flow, since the stock is down ~57% from highs and worth $104B. Couch Investor walks through the business: the Axon AI ad engine, the MAX supply-side auction layer, Adjust analytics, and the new e-commerce/consumer vertical that hit record advertiser spend in June 2026. Fundamentals look strong — 77% operating margin, 88% gross margin, revenue up 53% YoY to $1.92B — but Q2 marked the first miss vs own guidance in 14 quarters (FCF missed by ~29% on tax/interest timing, EBITDA missed ~1%), with management admitting Axon model lifts arrive unevenly and aren't guaranteed each quarter. He also revisits the overhang history: short-seller fraud allegations (Fuzzy Panda, Muddy Waters) and an SEC inquiry that has now closed. Bull case: growth, profitability, cheap at 17x forward PE with 67% EPS growth expected. Bear case: growth depends on unpredictable model breakthroughs, heavy mobile-gaming concentration, and Meta potentially re-entering in-app bidding. Conclusion: interesting to watch, but with Meta cheaper and better positioned in advertising, he does not need APP and does not see a credible road to $1T anytime soon.
title: Could This Be the Next Multibagger? One CEO Thinks So
